page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.m1.medium is an x86_64 virtual server provisioned through the KVM hypervisor. The hardware profile supplies 4 dedicated virtual CPUs and 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing a standard general-purpose ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance contains no integrated GPU accelerators and features dedicated CPU resource allocation, preventing cross-tenant processing contention.

The server configuration does not include local disk storage, which requires persistent storage and operating system images to be hosted on detached network-attached block volumes. Similarly, the instance is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating configured networking gateways or allocated elastic network interfaces for direct internet reachability.

With its balanced compute-to-memory ratio and dedicated virtual core profile, the ecs.m1.medium maintains a predictable performance model for mid-sized computing demands. It fits general-purpose production needs, including application backends, staging environments, distributed container workloads, and web serving clusters.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.m1.medium is a general-purpose virtual server built on the x86_64 architecture and deployed through the KVM hypervisor. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per virtual processor. The instance does not include dedicated graphics processing units and features no bundled local storage, requiring operators to attach network-based block storage volumes for system disks and operational data persistence. Network connectivity is delivered without complimentary public IPv4 addresses. By providing dedicated vCPU allocation, the instance avoids resource throttling typical of shared or burstable environments. The balanced resource ratio offers predictable resource utilization for standard computing requirements. The ecs.m1.medium is appropriate for general enterprise workloads, such as distributed application microservices, intermediate web application hosting, build systems, and staging environments.
